title: The Mysteries of Plato's Parmenides Dispersed: From musical intervals to contacts/"hapseis" to "logoi"
summary: Plato's Parmenides has long been considered the most difficult and enigmatic of Platonic dialogues, marked by seemingly contradictory arguments. We present an interpretation showing that the One of the Second Hypothesis (142b-155e) is an intelligible Being whose structure constitutes the philosophical analogue of a dyad in periodic anthyphairesis. First, by linguistic analysis and Proclus' Platonic Theology, we show that the One and the Being form an indefinite dyad satisfying the philosophical analogue of infinite anthyphairesis.
